column1: # Dead Wars: The Last Boat storylets - authoring guide: docs/tech/STORY.md
# one row per line of dialogue, in order; choice empty = before the menu, N = after choice N

column4: body
The pot is mostly water tonight. {res.food} rations left in the crates.
We can make this last, or we can eat like people. Not both.
Eat up. Tomorrow can worry about tomorrow.
Nobody says much. Spoons scrape the tin long after the bowls are empty.
Did I ever tell you about the wedding cake? The whole thing. By myself.
{A.name} checks the treeline. Deer tracks, fresh, heading down to the creek.
I can be back before dark. Probably.
One shot echoes off the hills. {A.name} comes back dragging a young doe.
{A.name} comes back late and scratched up, with two rabbits and a grin.
Fine. The tracks will still be there tomorrow. Maybe.
{B.name}, you sleep through your watch again and I leave you at the next stop.
Say it louder, Sergeant. Wake up the whole county.
{B.He} turn{B.s} {B.his} back on the fire. {B.He} {B.has} nothing more to say.
{A.name} storms off to check the cars. Again.
Somebody snorts. Then everybody is laughing, even {A.name}. Even {B.name}.
That's every night this week, {A.name}. Every night, somebody.
...Yeah. I hear it. I sound like my old man.
{A.name} sits by {A.self} for a long time. Something in {A.him} unclenches.
So, {A.name}. Where were you when it started?
Stuck in traffic with everybody else. I walked away from my car and never looked back.
{B.name} laughs. It's the first time {A.name} has heard {B.him} laugh.
Got something. Haven Bay harbor control. It's a recorded loop.
...last sailing in {days_left} days. Do not bring the bitten. Repeat, do not...
{days_left} days. We can make that. We can.
A woman waves from the shoulder, a boy limp in her arms. His leg is wrapped in a bloody shirt.
Pull over. Please. I can look at him.
It's a cut, not a bite. Keep it clean. Every day, you hear me? Every day.
{A.name} watches them shrink in the mirror and doesn't speak again until dark.
A man waves from the shoulder. Clean jacket, full duffel bag, nobody else around.
Nobody that clean is alone. We drive past, or we take the bag.
Listen to yourself, {A.name}. We're not bandits.
He doesn't fight. He just watches you go. The bag holds food and a box of shells.
Your call. When we're starving, remember whose call it was.
{A.name} spots a green cross through the trees. The pharmacy door hangs open.
Shelves could still be full. Could be full of them, too. Give me ten minutes.
Ten minutes. Twenty. Then {A.name} is back, out of breath, pockets rattling with pills.
Your call. I'd have been quick.
Sit down before you fall down, {A.name}.
I'm fine. I'm fine. I just need a minute.
Hold still. This is going to sting, and you're going to let it.
{B.name} stays with {A.him} until {A.his} hands stop shaking.
They raise a cairn for {A.name} at the edge of the road. {B.name} carries the top stone up from the river.
{A.He} pulled me out of that store on the first day. I never said thanks. Not once.
{B.name} sits by the cairn until the fire burns out.
We fought about everything. Every single thing. And now {A.he} {A.is} just gone.
I said things to {A.him} I can't take back. Not now. Not ever.
{B.name} nods, but doesn't look up.
{B.name} walks off alone. Nobody follows.
Teeth. Through the sleeve. I felt them go in.
{A.name} won't meet anyone's eyes.
I know what this means. I know how many days I have.
The camp goes quiet. Someone moves {A.name}'s bedroll to the far side of the fire.
{A.name} bites down on a belt while the knife heats. Nobody sleeps.
Not a word. Not yet. Let me think.
Let me see it, {A.name}. No, look at me. Not at the wound. At me.
Don't. You know what's coming. Don't get close.
Clean, dressed, and you're not alone. That buys time. Time is all we need.
{B.name} steps back. {A.name} sees it, and something in {A.his} face closes.
Two cans are gone from the crate. {B.name} finds the empty tins behind {A.name}'s bedroll.
You want to tell us something, {A.name}?
I was hungry. We're all hungry. I'm sorry, okay? I'm sorry.
{A.name} eats last tomorrow, and the day after. Nobody lets {A.him} forget it.
{A.name} mumbles a thank you. Nobody looks at {A.him} for the rest of the night.
Here. Take mine. Just ask next time. Ask, and I'll say yes.
{A.name} is burning up. Shivering, sweating, talking to people who aren't there.
No bite. I checked twice. It's just a fever. Just a fever.
{A.He} need{A.s} meds, or somebody awake beside {A.him} all night.
The pills go down on the third try. By morning {A.name} can hold a cup.
{B.name} wipes {A.name}'s face until dawn. Neither of them says much.
{A.name} thrashes until dawn. Then the fever breaks, and takes something with it.
{A.name} has {A.his} pack on and {A.his} boots laced. It's the middle of the night.
I'm faster alone. You're all going to die on this road, and I'm not staying to watch.
Then go. Or sit down for five minutes and let me talk.
We're slower together. We're also still alive together. Count how many people can say that.
{A.name} sits down. After a while, {A.he} take{A.s} the pack off.
An extra can of peaches does what words couldn't. {A.name} stays. For now.
{A.name} walks into the dark. An hour later {A.he} walk{A.s} back and sit{A.s} by the fire.
Nobody says anything. Nobody has to.
Leave me at the next town. I'm slowing you down, and I'm too tired to be scared anymore.
You're the only one of us who knows which end of the needle goes in.
Then I'll write it down for you. Please. I'm so tired.
...Fine. But I want the good blanket.
It's the closest thing to a joke {A.he} {A.has} made in a month.
{A.name} sleeps for fourteen hours. Everyone else stands {A.his} watch.
{A.name} and {B.name} take the same watch. They don't talk much. They don't need to.
When this is over... if it's ever over... I'd like to keep doing this. Watches. With you.
{A.name} doesn't answer. {A.He} just move{A.s} closer to the fire, and to {B.name}.
{B.name}. Over here. You hold that like it owes you money.
Breathe out. Squeeze, don't pull. And never shoot when walking away will do.
Two shots echo down the valley. The second one hits the can.
Huh. Not bad. Not bad at all.
An hour of click, click, click. {B.name}'s finger aches. {B.His} grip doesn't shake.
{B.name}. If I get bitten... you don't let me turn. You don't let me hurt anyone.
Don't. Don't ask me that.
I'm asking. Promise me. And I'll promise you the same.
...Okay. I promise. And you promise me.
They shake on it like it's a business deal. Neither one lets go for a while.
No. If one of us gets bitten, the other one finds a cure. That's the promise. Both of us.
How many days?
Enough to see a few more sunsets. Don't make that face.
{B.name} stays until {A.name} falls asleep. Then a while longer.
{A.name} wakes screaming. Out in the dark, something answers.
Shh. Shh. You're here. You're with us. Breathe.
{B.name} holds on until the shaking stops. Maybe the worst of it has passed. Maybe.
A rag, a belt, and a long night. {A.name} won't look at {B.name} in the morning.
Everyone else sleeps, at least.
Wait. Listen. Somebody left a station on automatic. It's been playing the same tape for weeks.
Old dance music crackles out of the speaker. {B.name} groans. Then {B.he} start{B.s} tapping {B.his} foot.
By the third song everyone is dancing badly in the firelight. Even the ones who swore they wouldn't.
A boat. On a tape. You know what a tape proves? That somebody once owned a tape recorder.
Then why are you still walking?
Same reason as you. Nowhere else to walk.
{A.name} shrugs and rolls over. The fire pops. Nobody sleeps well.
...Yeah. Yeah, maybe.
The camp gets very quiet after that.
There's a house down the hill with the curtains still drawn. I'm going in tonight.
In the dark. Alone. With them out there.
That's what makes it fun.
{A.name} slips off into the dark. {A.He} come{A.s} back at dawn with a sack of cans and a look you don't ask about.
Two shadows go down the hill. Two come back at dawn, loaded down. {B.name} is limping a little.
Fine. Babysit me. See if I care.
{A.name} takes the first watch. Then the second. Then the third.
Sleep. All of you. I'll wake you if anything moves.
{B.name} catches {A.name} counting pills into {A.his} palm. Not for a patient.
They take the edges off. Just the edges. I'm still a doctor. I'm still fine.
{A.name} hands the bag over. {A.His} hands are shaking. So are {B.name}'s.
{B.name} looks away. In the morning the edges are gone, and so is the old tired look.
They talk until the fire is coals. {A.name} puts the pills back, one at a time.
The med count is off again. {B.name} doesn't need to ask who.
{A.name}. Those are for when someone's bleeding.
Someone is bleeding. You just can't see where.
{B.name} rigs a lock on the med box. {A.name} watches {B.him} do it and says nothing.
Nobody says anything. In the morning the count is off by one more.
The dog watches every spoon, from bowl to mouth and back again.
We can't feed it. We can barely feed us. You all know what I'm going to say next.
Somebody's portion gets a little smaller. The dog sleeps against {A.name}'s legs.
{A.name} walks the dog a mile back down the road and runs. It doesn't follow. That's the worst part.
Nobody talks during dinner. It tastes like nothing. Everyone eats anyway.
{A.name} hasn't gone near the treeline since the last fight. Not even to pee.
Come on. Watch with me tonight. Just the two of us. Nothing's going to happen.
Nothing happens. All night, nothing happens, and {A.name} is there for every minute of it.
In the morning {A.he} walk{A.s} to the treeline alone. Just to see if {A.he} can.
{A.name} sleeps in the car with the doors locked. Nobody blames {A.him}. Not out loud.
Steam pours out from under the lead car's hood. The engine coughs twice and dies.
Radiator hose. I can patch it if we have parts. Or I can get creative with tape and prayer.
Twenty minutes, one new hose, and a lot of swearing. The engine turns over.
Tape, wire, a sock and a bent spoon. It holds. Mostly. It drips a little.
The engine wheezes along at twenty miles an hour, drinking fuel the whole way.
A body lies face down in the ditch. Hiking boots. A full backpack. Flies, but not many.
Not many flies means not dead long. Or not dead enough.
{A.name} rolls it over. Its eyes are open. For a second, nobody breathes.
{A.name} puts the knife in first, just to be sure. Then {A.he} open{A.s} the pack.
Yeah. Let somebody else find out.
Ahead, the road is moving. Hundreds of them, shuffling across from one field to the next.
We can wait them out, go around through the fields, or put our foot down and punch through.
Four hours of waiting with the engines off. Everyone eats. Nobody talks above a whisper.
The cars bounce across a mile of plowed field. Somebody throws up. You make it.
Bodies thump off the bumper. Something claws at {A.name}'s window. Then you're through.
A school bus blocks the road. Three rifles behind it. A painted sign: TOLL.
Food or bullets, friends. Pay up, or we take the lot and the cars with it.
They've got the high ground. Your call.
Three cans go over the hood of the bus. The rifles follow you all the way past.
A box of shells changes hands. One of them tips his hat. You want to hit him.
We've got sick people and nothing worth your bullets. Let us by and we forget your faces.
A long pause. Then the bus rolls back six feet. Just enough.
Glass explodes. Somebody screams. Then you are past them, and the bus is burning in the mirror.
A rifle shot stars the windshield. Behind you, a school bus with a burned hood, closing fast.
They remember us. Heads down!
The cars scrape past the ditch at sixty. Something tears loose underneath. You lose them.
{A.name} leans out the window and fires twice. The bus swerves into the ditch and stays there.
A skinny dog trots alongside the caravan for a mile. Then two. It won't quit.
Look at those ribs. Somebody's going to feed that dog, and I think it's me.
The dog eats from {A.name}'s hand, then climbs into the back seat like it owns the car.
The dog keeps up for another mile. Then it stops in the road and watches you go.
A man thumbs a ride at the crossroads. His left sleeve is soaked dark and tied off at the elbow.
It's a cut. I swear on my kids it's a cut. Please.
It's not a cut.
You leave him a can of beans and a bottle of water. He's still waving when the road bends.
Nobody looks back. {A.name} keeps {A.his} eyes on the road for a long, long time.
{A.name} does it quickly, then sits in the car without starting it for a while.
A minivan sits in the breakdown lane, doors open, keys in. Crayon drawings taped to the back window.
Tank's half full. Somebody hand me the hose.
{A.name} gets a mouthful of gasoline. Again. But the cans fill up.
The Haven Bay loop is gone. Just static. Since this morning.
Could be the antenna. Could be the hills. Could be...
{A.name} spends the whole drive with the headphones on, turning the dial a hair at a time.
Wait. Wait! Everybody shut up!
...boarding continues at Haven Bay. Last sailing in {days_left} days. Repeat...
{A.name} is crying and laughing at the same time. Nobody makes fun of {A.him} for it.
A girl waves from the shoulder, crying. The grass in the ditch behind her is flattened in too many places.
Don't stop. Look at the ditch. That's an ambush.
In the mirror, three men climb out of the ditch and stand in the road, watching you go.
Men come out of the ditch with bats. They grab what they can before {A.name} gets the car moving.
The church door is chained shut. Taped to it: hundreds of notes. Names. Photos. GONE TO HAVEN BAY.
We should leave one. So somebody knows we came through.
{A.name} writes every name in the caravan, living and dead, and tapes it in the middle.
The pews are good dry oak and the hinges are brass. Nobody prays. Somebody apologizes.
Behind a burned-out house, a vegetable garden has gone wild. Tomatoes. Beans. Something like squash.
Give me an hour and a sack.
Something moves in the corn rows. {A.name} keeps picking, one eye on the stalks.
{A.name} fills {A.his} pockets from the edge and backs away from the tall corn.
Sandbags. A burned army truck. A hand-painted sign: NO BITTEN BEYOND THIS POINT.
Third Battalion. My old unit. Somebody gave them an order they never should have followed.
The trailer might still have something in it. Or we leave them be.
Two crates of rifle rounds, and a logbook. {A.name} reads the last page and then burns it.
{A.name} stands at the sandbags for a minute. Then {A.he} salute{A.s} and walk{A.s} back to the car.
The school still has its banner up: WELCOME BACK, STUDENTS! The front doors are chained from the outside.
On the windows, kids' drawings. Houses, suns, dogs. People with red mouths.
There's a nurse's office, and a broken side window. If we can stand to walk through there.
{A.name} comes back with a box of bandages and doesn't say a word about the classrooms.
Yeah. No. Some doors stay shut.
A fuel tanker lies on its side across two lanes. You can smell it a block away.
If the valve's not cracked, there's a lot of gas in there. If it is, nobody lights a match.
Twenty minutes of nobody breathing. The cans fill. {A.name}'s hands smell like gas for days.
Fair. I like my eyebrows where they are.
A jewelry store. The front window is smashed, but the back cases are still locked.
Gold. When this is over, gold's going to matter again. Give me five minutes.
When this is over? Look around you.
{A.name} comes out with a pocket of rings, a drawer of watchmaker's tools, and a new cut on {A.his} arm.
{B.name} hauls {A.name} out by the collar. {A.name} sulks for the rest of the day.
Back at the cars, somebody starts laughing. It catches, the way it does when you've been that scared.
Good work. All of you. Now let's be gone before they come looking.
{B.name}! You were supposed to cover the left side! Where were you?
Where was I? Where were you, while you were busy being a hero?
It goes on until somebody walks away. Nobody remembers who.
That one's on me. I picked the wrong way in, and you paid for it.
Tomorrow we do it smarter. Get some sleep.
Rounds left: {res.ammo}. That's it. That's the whole war chest.
From here on, it's knives and clubs. Guns are for when it all goes wrong.
{A.name} spends the evening teaching everyone how to swing a pipe without losing it.
Powder, primers, a vise and a lot of patience. By midnight, a few more rounds.
Halfway through stitching {B.name}'s scrape, {A.name} starts laughing and can't stop.
Sorry. Sorry. I just realized I haven't filled out a single form in two months. It's wonderful.
Something in {A.name} has come unstuck. {A.He} hum{A.s} while {A.he} work{A.s}.
{A.name} hasn't said a word since the fight. {A.His} hands won't stop shaking.
I froze. Right out in the open. I could hear it coming and I couldn't move. Me.
Something that held {A.name} together all this way has cracked. Everyone can see it.
They raise a marker facing the road ahead. {A.name} never once turned {A.his} back on it.
Never ran. Not once. Carve that on it.
{B.name} folds {A.name}'s blanket under the marker. {A.He}'d have given it away anyway.
{A.He} patched up every one of us. Who patches us up now?
{B.name} takes the med bag. Nobody argues.
{A.He} picked a fight with everything. The road, the dead, me. Mostly me.
And {A.he} never lost one. Not until today.
{B.name} carves {A.name}'s name into the marker with a knife. Crooked, the way {A.he}'d have done it.
They pile stones by the road, one for every day {A.name} made it.
Somebody should say something.
{A.name}. You made it further than most. Rest now. We'll take it from here.
{A.His} pack is still in the car. Half a box of shells. {A.name} won't need them. It still feels like stealing.
{A.name}. You did your job. You can stand down now.
{B.name} says the soldier's words over the stones. Nobody else knows them. Nobody interrupts.
I'm adding {A.name} to the list. When the radio works, I read the list out loud.
Somebody out there should know {A.he} lived. Not just that {A.he} died.
Well. That's one less mouth to feed.
{C.name} hits {B.him}. Hard. Nobody pulls the two of them apart for a while.
I'm keeping {A.his} spare knife. {A.He}'d want it to keep working.
{B.name} wears it on {B.his} belt from then on, and checks it's there a hundred times a day.
Eight years in the ER. I've lost people before. It never felt like this.
Like it was my fault. Like I wasn't watching.
{B.name} nods like {B.he} believe{B.s} it. {B.He} sit{B.s} up the rest of the night anyway.
{B.name} goes through the med bag by firelight, item by item, until {B.he} know{B.s} it blind.
{A.name} keeps {A.his} sleeve pulled down all the way back to the cars. In this heat.
Roll it up, {A.name}. Now. Let me see.
It's nothing. I fell. It's a scrape. Please don't.
{B.name} says it out loud. Nobody sits near {A.name} at dinner.
Okay. But you tell me if it gets worse. Swear it.
Don't let me turn. Not tonight, not tomorrow. Now, while I'm still me.
There's still time. There's meds, there's...
{B.name}. Look at me. Please.
{B.name} does it quickly. Then {B.he} sit{B.s} in the dirt beside {A.name} for a long time.
Not yet. Not while there's a chance. Don't you dare give up on me.
There are things we haven't tried. Bleed it. Burn it. Pack it with every antibiotic we have.
Will it work?
I don't know. Nobody knows. That's the whole point of trying.
It takes all night and all of {A.name}'s screaming. In the morning, nobody knows yet.
...You're right. I'm sorry. I just wanted to do something.
Listen to me. The bite is below the joint. If I take the limb tonight, above it, you live.
And if I say no?
Then I sit with you. Until.
{A.name} nods. Somebody starts boiling water. Somebody else finds a belt to bite on.
No. I'd rather go whole. Don't ask me again.
It's a scratch! I've had worse from a cat! Stop looking at me like that!
{A.name} punches the car door hard enough to dent it. {B.name} doesn't flinch.
Nobody's looking. Sit down before you break your hand.
{B.name}. You're in charge now. If I start acting funny, you don't wait for orders.
{A.name} hands over {A.his} rifle, stock first. {B.name} has never seen {A.his} hands shake before.
{A.name}. I made you a promise. By the fire. I remember.
So do I. So keep it.
{B.name} keeps it. Quickly, the way they agreed. Then {B.he} sit{B.s} with {A.name} until it's dark.
I promised you a cure. I'm going to find it. You hold on until I do.
Not yet. Not today. Ask me again tomorrow.
{A.name}. I made you a promise. By the fire. I remember.
So do I. So keep it.
{B.name} keeps it. Quickly, the way they agreed. Then {B.he} sit{B.s} with {A.name} until it's dark.
I promised you a cure. I'm going to find it. You hold on until I do.
Not yet. Not today. Ask me again tomorrow.
Past midnight the dog stands up, hackles raised, growling low at the dark.
Douse the fire. Nobody move. Nobody breathe.
Shapes drift past the camp, close enough to smell. Then they're gone. The dog gets the last of the stew.
Hear that knock? That's your fuel going out the tailpipe. Give me an hour and a wrench.
There. She'll sip it now instead of guzzling it. You're welcome.
Your funeral. Literally, probably.
You don't even believe in the boat. Why are you still here?
I don't believe in the boat. I believe in you idiots. Somebody has to keep your cars running.
{A.name} goes back to the engine before anyone can see {A.his} face.
Under {A.name}'s bedroll, {B.name} finds granola bars, a jar of peanut butter and three cans of peaches.
What? I've been on my own since I was fourteen. You learn to keep a little back.
{A.name} dumps it all in the crate and doesn't speak to anyone until morning.
...Thanks. I'll share the peaches. Maybe.
Give me ten minutes. I'll go over the rooftops and see what's waiting for us.
{A.name} is back in eight, grinning, with a pocket of shotgun shells and a map drawn on {A.his} arm.
Fine. Slow and safe. My favorite. Said nobody.
